transcript.text: We had a power cut last night and now our Candy washer dryer is completely dead - no lights, nothing. Everything else in the house came back on. The plug fuse is fine, I swapped it. Help!

A power cut can sometimes cause a surge that blows an internal safety fuse (thermal cut-out) inside the machine, even if the plug fuse is fine. The next step is to rule out the socket and reset any transient lockout. Please unplug the machine for 30 seconds, then plug it back in firmly into a different wall socket if possible (or ensure the current one is live by testing with a lamp). If there are still no lights after this, we will need to check the internal power supply.
[Safety panel] An appliance that keeps tripping your electrics — or that smells of burning or has scorch marks — may have an electrical fault. Stop using it, switch it off and unplug it, don't keep resetting it, and have it checked by a qualified electrician or appliance engineer.
I've already unplugged it for over 10 minutes and it was still dead. I tested the socket with a lamp and that works fine. No burning smell either. What next?

Since the socket and external fuse are fine, the issue is likely an internal safety component that opened during the surge. The most common cause in Candy washer-dryers after a power cut is the internal mains fuse blowing on the PCB or within the mains lead assembly itself. Please check if the cable enters securely at the back of the machine; if it feels loose or damaged, replacing the lead may solve it. If the connection looks solid, we need to verify if electricity is actually reaching the inside of the machine by checking for continuity in the plug/cable assembly.
[Safety panel] An appliance that keeps tripping your electrics — or that smells of burning or has scorch marks — may have an electrical fault. Stop using it, switch it off and unplug it, don't keep resetting it, and have it checked by a qualified electrician or appliance engineer.

The cable and plug look fine, no damage, and it's firmly in at the plug end. I'm not comfortable taking the back panel off or testing anything internal though. Is there anything else I can try, or should I get an engineer in? It might still be under an extended warranty.

There is nothing further you can safely do at home. The power cut likely blew an internal safety fuse or damaged a component on the main circuit board, which requires specialist tools to diagnose and replace. You should contact Candy support or your warranty provider to arrange an engineer visit, as this is not a user-serviceable fault.
